description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange) and SESHA ft model (green)—compared to the Whisper large model, across five different optimisations applied to the data: Dates, Americanisms, Remove Spacing, Add Spacing, and Normalised. The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large," with values ranging from 0.000 to 0.004, while the vertical axis lists the optimisations applied. For each optimisation, two bars are displayed side-by-side, with the NESAC ft model consistently showing a higher WER difference than the SESHA ft model. The highest difference in WER is observed for the "Add Spacing" optimisation, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00319 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00344. The lowest difference is for the "Dates" optimisation, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00257 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00228. The chart includes a legend at the bottom indicating the model colors.
